newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent faces resistance at $19.64, $19.78.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent faces resistance at $19.64, $19.78.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ IPE Brent faces initial resistance at $19.64 then a stronger obstacle at $19.78-$19.80.
+ Gas oil faces continuation chart resistance at $179.50 and then September chart resistance at $180-$180.50.
IPE Brent crude oil futures face nearby resistance on Wednesday at the top of Monday's trading range at $19.64 a barrel and then a stronger barrier up at $19.78-$19.80, technical analysts said.
September Brent closed six cents a barrel firmer on Tuesday at $19.52, following a sharp 51 cent rise on Monday, while August gas oil was four dollars a tonne up at $176.25.
Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson Derivatives on the Isle of Man said he was looking for the market to test resistance based on a double top from early June at $19.78-80.
"We have been looking for it to test that but I don't think it is going to be broken," he said. "There is a fair chance it will even test that today."
He said that if prices did break through this barrier, however, the next important resistance level would be encountered at the May 16 peak of $20.40.

Support would be found at the top of the previous trading range at $19.00, he added. "In the longer term the downside support is at $17.68 to $17.85. These latter two numbers correspond to chart troughs on June 20 and July 14.
"The trend on Brent and gas oil is down and we should test the highs in the next few days and test the bottom over several weeks."
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International said in a daily report he saw resistance for Brent at $19.64.
"I'm looking to get real bearish on Wednesday at above $19.64." Above that lies $19.97 and strong resistance at $20.37, he said, and pegged support at $19.30-$19.22, then $19.09-$18.80.
Wilson said gas oil faced important resistance at an island reversal gap on the September chart at $180.00-$180.50, formed in mid- to late-May.
"I think we will fill that gap but I don't see the market going through the high at $183.25."
On the downside he saw support at the early June chart gap from $175.75-$174.75 and at this week's gap between $174.75 and $176.50.
"We will find initial support at that gap and then we should test the old trading range," he said, adding that the bottom of that lay at around $162.
Dealers also expected strong resistance on the gas oil, too, at $179.50, the peak reached on the continuation chart on May 22.
